title: The project
text:
GEMS is an open-science project for brief cognitive assessment. It started with the paper-and-pencil GEMS (2022) and grew into a family of tools for in-person, telephone and web-based screening. The work is a collaboration between the University of Padua and IRCCS San Camillo Hospital in Venice, within the NICLA group.


All materials are on the Open Science Framework (OSF) under a Creative Commons licence: record forms, instructions, scoring sheets, analysis code and Shiny apps for the cut-offs.

GEMS: osf.io/4t5a8
Tele-GEMS: osf.io/t3bma
Auto-GEMS: osf.io/fq8g7




Open materials make it easy to translate GEMS and collect normative data in other countries. Each test on this site has one page per language, marked by a flag. New languages are added as translations become available.
If you would like to translate, adapt or norm GEMS in your language, contact us. We are happy to support cross-cultural validation projects.

title: Global Examination of Mental State
text:
Open-access cognitive screening

Global Examination of Mental State

Three free, validated tools for the brief assessment of cognition: in person, by telephone, or self-administered on the web. Each comes with normative data, cut-offs that account for cognitive reserve, and all materials needed to use it.







In person · paper and pencil

GEMS


A paper-and-pencil screening of global cognition with 11 tasks covering orientation, memory, attention, visuo-spatial skills, language and pragmatics. It takes about 10 minutes.



 

Learn more →




Remote · telephone

Tele-GEMS


The telephone version of GEMS for remote screening, with 10 tasks that mirror the in-person test. It takes about 10 minutes.



 

Learn more →




Self-administered · web

Auto-GEMS


A self-administered web version that runs in any browser, online or offline, and compares the result with the normative data automatically. It takes about 10 minutes.





Learn more →







Free and open
Record forms, instructions, scoring sheets and code are released under a Creative Commons licence on OSF.





Large normative samples
The norms are based on 600 to 1,300 healthy adults per test, covering the adult lifespan.





Cognitive reserve
The cut-offs account for age, sex, education and the Cognitive Reserve Index (CRIq).





Built for follow-up
Parallel forms A and B and significant-change thresholds support repeated assessments.

title: About GEMS
text:
The Global Examination of Mental State (GEMS) is a family of brief cognitive screening tools. They give a quick, reliable picture of a person’s global cognitive functioning when a full neuropsychological assessment is not needed or not possible.


Many screenings are tuned to a single condition, show ceiling effects in healthy people, or rely on norms that are outdated or not freely available. GEMS was designed to address these issues:

Broad coverage. Orientation, memory, working memory, visuo-spatial and planning abilities, attention, language and pragmatics, in about 10 minutes.
No ceiling effect in healthy adults, so differences between individuals remain visible.
Cognitive reserve. Cut-offs consider the Cognitive Reserve Index (CRIq) together with age, sex and education, so expectations are more precise than with education alone.
Repeated testing. Parallel forms and significant-change thresholds support longitudinal monitoring.
Open materials. Record forms, instructions, scoring sheets and code are free under a Creative Commons licence.

The three versions share the same structure, so results can be compared across settings. For example, a patient first seen in person can be followed up remotely.



GEMS tools are screenings. They do not replace a comprehensive neuropsychological assessment and should be interpreted by qualified professionals.
